ai.description: *Micrixalus kurichiyari* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored belly. It is distinguished by a prominent, pale-spotted throat and the male's characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus kurichiyari* is best distinguished by its unique, vibrant orange-red dorsal coloration, which contrasts sharply with the duller, mottled patterns of other dancing frogs.
ai.habitat: The Kurichiyar Dancing Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky, fast-flowing streams at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, male Kurichiyar dancing frogs perform rhythmic hind-limb extensions, known as "foot-flagging," to attract mates and signal rivals near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Kurichiyar Dancing Frog breeds during the monsoon season (June–August). Females lay small clutches of approximately 15–20 large, unpigmented eggs in stream-bed burrows.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kurichiyar dancing frog is endemic to the Wayanad district in Kerala, India, where it inhabits high-elevation streams within the Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The Kurichiyar Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short "tink" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing rocky streams in its forest habitat.
